# Food Storage Guide

> A free, multilingual reference for how long food keeps in the pantry, the
> refrigerator and the freezer, and how to store it properly. Traditional
> Chinese, English, Japanese and Spanish.

Storage timelines are derived from the USDA FSIS FoodKeeper dataset (public
domain, https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/fsis-foodkeeper-data). Food-safety
principles follow published guidance from the USDA, FDA, CDC, WHO, UK FSA,
Taiwan TFDA, Japan's Consumer Affairs Agency and Spain's AESAN. Foods absent
from FoodKeeper are researched separately and cite their sources on the page.

Timelines indicate best quality unless stated otherwise. Refrigerated raw meat,
seafood and prepared dishes are the exception, where the timeline is a safety
limit. Food held continuously at -18 C stays microbiologically safe
indefinitely.

## Key reference points
- Refrigerator: 4 C (40 F) or below. Taiwan TFDA commonly cites 7 C; Japanese
  food hygiene rules define refrigeration as 10 C or below.
- Freezer: -18 C (0 F).
- Danger zone: 4-60 C (40-140 F).
- Two-hour rule: discard perishable food left in the danger zone for more than
  2 hours, or 1 hour above 32 C (90 F).
- Reheat leftovers to 74 C (165 F).

## Sections
- /zh, /en, /ja, /es: localised home pages with search
- /{locale}/foods: full food index with pantry, fridge and freezer times
- /{locale}/category/{category}: one of vegetables, fruits, meat, poultry,
  seafood, dairy-eggs, grains-beans-pasta, baked-goods, baking-staples,
  condiments-sauces, herbs-spices, oils-fats, shelf-stable, snacks-nuts-seeds,
  beverages, frozen-foods, deli-prepared, vegetarian-proteins, baby-food
- /{locale}/food/{slug}: one food, with storage times, spoilage signs, thawing
  and FAQ
- /{locale}/guides and /{locale}/guides/{slug}: food-safety guide articles with
  cited sources
- /{locale}/methodology: how the data is sourced and processed

## Citation
Cite as "Food Storage Guide" with a link to the specific page. The underlying
USDA FoodKeeper data is public domain; the written explanations, guides and
translations are original work.
